findings.title: New `cf validate frontmatter` command implements the documented 0/1/2 exit-code contract and JSON shape
findings.description: `validateFrontmatterAction` resolves the project via the shared `resolveProjectWorktree`, calls the core `validateFrontmatterFiles` service (no duplicated discovery/validation logic), applies `fixAction`s in a single pass with one per-run date stamp, and emits the JSON shape from slice 923's A3 spec (`filesChecked`, `totalFindings`, `errors`, `warnings`, `findings`, plus `fixed`/`fixLog`/`fixErrors` in fix mode). Error handling is per the project rules: per-fix `try/catch` is a documented specific-exception path (failure collected, reported, and reflected in the exit code, not swallowed), and the action-level catch is a process boundary delegating to `handleError(err, 2)`. Verified against `packages/core/src/introspection/writers/markdownWriter.ts` and the 923 slice design — the stamp semantics and the no-`dateUpdated` machine-artifact schemas are consistent end to end.

findings.title: `handleError` gains a backward-compatible exit-code parameter with corrected docs
findings.description: The change from a hard-coded `process.exit(1)` to `process.exit(exitCode)` with a default of `1` is the minimal change; the doc comment now says "exits with the given code" instead of the old (now-wrong) "exits with code 1". All existing single-argument callers across `packages/cli/src` are unchanged, and the new default also means the top-level `uncaughtException`/`unhandledRejection` handlers keep their historical code 1.

findings.title: Schema registration for the three machine-artifact docTypes is correct and the test suite pins the asymmetry
findings.description: The three schemas carry exactly `docType` + `dateCreated`, and I verified in `validateFrontmatter` (step 3) that the `dateUpdated`-backfill only fires for *required* fields, so the comment's claim — "requiring the field would make the existing backfill manufacture a false claim" — is accurate. The pre-existing "every schema requires docType, status, dateCreated, dateUpdated" tests were narrowed to the 8 canonical `EXPECTED_DOC_TYPES` rather than deleted or weakened, and a new test asserts the machine-artifact field set exactly (`['dateCreated', 'docType']`), which keeps the no-`dateUpdated` rule enforced. The unknown-docType fall-through is unchanged and explicitly documented.

findings.title: CLI tests follow the testing rules (vitest, centralized tests/, boundary mocks, one concept per test)
findings.description: The test file lives in `packages/cli/tests/commands/` matching the source module name (centralized layout, not colocated `__tests__`), uses vitest, mocks only the package boundary (`@context-forge/core/node`) with the same `vi.fn()`-per-function pattern as the established `check.test.ts`, uses `program.exitOverride()` so `process.exit(2)` is assertable, resets `process.exitCode` in `beforeEach`, and each test asserts one behavior. The `expect(dateStampArg).toMatch(/^\d{8}$/)` assertion pins the composed #71+#73 guarantee (real `formatDateProject` output passed as the fourth writer argument) rather than implementation detail. No DB access anywhere in the tier (pure fs/core, and the core-side tests use throwaway `mkdtemp` dirs they clean up), so the prod-URL guard rules are not triggered.
